entities.summary: Fiji is a sovereign nation in Melanesia, Oceania. Its capital is Suva. Official languages include English, Fijian (iTaukei), Fiji Hindi. Government: Unitary parliamentary republic. Population: approximately 0.9 million. Area: 18,274 km². Comprehensive index for Fiji covering Lapita people settlement (~1500 BCE), Melanesian/Polynesian chiefdoms, cannibalism era ('Cannibal Isles'), European contact (Abel Tasman 1643, Cook 1774), Cakobau unification, cession to Britain 1874, indentured Indian labour (girmitiya 1879-1916), independence 1970, coups (1987 Rabuka x2, 2000 Speight, 2006 Bainimarama), ethnic tensions (indigenous vs Indo-Fijian), 2013 constitution, return to democracy.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Fiji's history of cannibalism and European contact had significant regional impact on Melanesian societies. The country's independence in 1970 marked a major turning point for Pacific Island nations seeking self-determination.
